problems.title: Problem 1
problems.problem:
The arrangement in the figure is part of the drawing of the electric circuit of a car. The 3-position switch (δ) is initially set to contact (1), so that the charge of the capacitor is $q_1 = Q$. Then it closes contact (2) and the charge is now $q_2 = 1.2Q$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2026-2-1-fig1.png

(a) Find the internal resistance of the electric source as a function of the resistance $R$.

(b) When the switch is moved to contact (3), what will then be the value of the charge $q_3$?

[2×10 = 20 marks]

problems.title: Problem 2
problems.problem:
A firefighting aeroplane is equipped with the Hephaesnus system, which uses projectiles with biodegradable chemicals that release their extinguishing load on impact at a seat of fire that cannot be approached in any other way. The aeroplane flies horizontally with constant velocity $\upsilon_1 = 40\,\mathrm{\frac{m}{s}}$ at a height $H$ above the horizontal ground. As it heads towards the seat of the fire and is at the beginning of a slope of inclination $\theta = 35^\circ$, it launches, with horizontal velocity $\upsilon_2 = 30\,\mathrm{\frac{m}{s}}$ relative to the aeroplane, a projectile that performs a horizontal projectile motion and lands on the seat of the fire in a direction perpendicular to the surface of the slope. Find:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2026-2-2-fig1.png

(a) The height $H$.

(b) The distance of the aeroplane from the seat of the fire at the moment the projectile strikes the ground.

(c) The position of the seat of the fire on the slope.

(d) The velocity with which the projectile reaches the seat of the fire. The air resistance on the motion of the projectile is negligible.

Given: $\tan 35^\circ = 0.7$, $g = 10\,\mathrm{\frac{m}{s^2}}$.

[4×5 = 20 marks]

problems.title: Problem 3
problems.problem:
Two tennis balls, each of mass $m = 60\,\mathrm{g}$ and diameter $d = 7\,\mathrm{cm}$, are released at a distance $r = 1\,\mathrm{m}$ between their centres, to move freely because of the universal gravitational attraction between them and without the presence of any other force or force field. In how much time will the two balls collide?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2026-2-3-fig1.png

Choose the correct answer [5 marks] with some justification of your choice [15 marks].

Given $G = 6.67\cdot10^{-11}\,\mathrm{\frac{m^3}{kg\cdot s^2}}$.

(A) In a few minutes.

(B) In a few days.

(C) In a few months.

(D) In a few years.

problems.title: Problem 4
problems.problem:
The air ioniser of an air conditioner filters particles of dust, pollen and other airborne allergens using an arrangement such as that in the figure. The air enters the ioniser with speed $\upsilon = 5\,\mathrm{\frac{m}{s}}$ and is forced to pass through a very thin, charged wire mesh, so that during the passage the particles acquire electric charge. Then the air stream with the particles is led between the parallel, oppositely charged plates of a collector, and so the particles are deflected from their path and are trapped in the filter that is on the plate they strike.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2026-2-4-fig1.png

Consider a pollen particle of radius $r = 10\,\mathrm{\mu m}$, mass $m = 4\cdot10^{-13}\,\mathrm{kg}$ and charge $q = 4.8\cdot10^{-16}\,\mathrm{C}$ that enters at the middle of the separation of the field of the plates, which have length $\ell = 20\,\mathrm{cm}$ and are a distance $d = 2\,\mathrm{cm}$ apart, in a direction parallel to the plates.

(a) Find the minimum voltage between the plates so that the particle is trapped by the filter. $g = 10\,\mathrm{\frac{m}{s^2}}$ [5 marks]

(b) Find the velocity of the particle at the moment it reaches the filter.

(c) According to Stokes' law, the particle, as it moves in the air stream, experiences a drag force $F = -(6\pi n r)\upsilon$, where $n = 1.8\cdot10^{-8}\,\mathrm{\frac{kg}{m\cdot s}}$ is the coefficient of "viscosity" and $\upsilon$ the speed of the stream. [5 marks]

(c1) Can the value of this force be considered negligible compared with the other forces acting on the particle? [5 marks]

(c2) If we also take into account the value of this force, with its initial value at entry taken as constant, must we increase or decrease the value of the voltage, and by how much, so that the particle is trapped in the filter? [5 marks]

problems.title: Problem 5A
problems.problem:
Using the arrangement in the photograph, we release the metal sphere so that it moves along the curved track starting from its upper end. When the sphere reaches the lower end of the track (point O), it passes through the photogate with horizontal velocity $\upsilon_0$. Point O is at a height $h$ above the ground. We assume that air resistance is negligible.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2026-2-5-fig1.jpg

The initial velocity of the horizontal projectile motion (the velocity with which the sphere passes the photogate) is calculated from the relation $\upsilon_0 = \frac{d}{\Delta t}$, where the reading $\Delta t$ of the timer is the time for which the sphere shades the photogate and $d = 0.015\,\mathrm{m}$ is the diameter of the sphere. In the calculations, round to two decimal places. Each time you measure the height from which the horizontal projectile motion starts, the range, and the time interval recorded by the photogate.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2026-2-5-fig2.png

Repeating the experiment 5 times, we recorded the values in the TABLE.

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c} \text{Height } h\ (\mathrm{m}) & \text{Range } x_{\max}\ (\mathrm{m}) & x_{\max}^2\ (\mathrm{m^2}) & \text{Time interval } \Delta t\ (\mathrm{s}) & \text{Initial velocity } \upsilon_0\ (\mathrm{\frac{m}{s}}) \\ \hline 0.50 & 0.37 & & 0.013 & \\ 0.40 & 0.32 & & 0.013 & \\ 0.30 & 0.28 & & 0.013 & \\ 0.20 & 0.23 & & 0.013 & \\ 0.10 & 0.16 & & 0.013 & \\ 0.00 & 0.00 & 0.00 & - & - \end{array}$$

Questions on the experimental procedure that follows:

(a) Fill in the blanks of the TABLE, rounding to two decimal places. [2 marks]

(b) Using the principle of independence of motions, write the equations of motion of the sphere as functions of time, on the horizontal and on the vertical axis, justifying your answer. [2 marks]

(c) By eliminating time, calculate the relation of height to the square of the range, $h(x_{\max}^2)$, and draw its graph. [2 marks]

(d) Calculate the slope of the graph to two decimal places, specifying its unit of measurement. [2 marks]

(e) Calculate the acceleration of gravity from the slope of the graph. The initial velocity is the mean value of the initial velocities in the TABLE. [1 mark]

(f) Why do the initial velocities in the TABLE have approximately the same value, although they were measured at different values of the height? [1 mark]

problems.title: Problem 5B: Study of a potato battery
problems.problem:
Study of a potato battery

We cut a thick slice of potato. In its upper part we screw in a galvanised screw and next to it we wedge a piece of copper. Our battery is ready.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2026-2-6-fig1.jpg

We want to study the battery we have made, that is, to determine its internal resistance and its electromotive force, to plot its characteristic and to find the maximum power that this particular battery produces.

From its study we obtained the following measurements, which are recorded in the table below.

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c} \text{Ohmic resistance of conductor in } \mathrm{k\Omega} & \text{Voltage across the battery in } \mathrm{V} & \text{Current in the circuit in } \mathrm{\mu A} & \text{Power delivered by the battery to the circuit in } \mathrm{\mu W} \\ \hline \text{Without resistor} & 0.93 & 0 & \\ 20 & 0.74 & 37 & \\ 10 & 0.61 & 60 & \\ 5 & 0.46 & 90 & \\ 2 & 0.28 & 133 & \\ 1 & 0.17 & 155 & \\ 0.5 & 0.10 & 168 & \end{array}$$

1. What other instruments and materials do you think were used for this study? Draw the circuit with which the above measurements were obtained. [2 marks]

2. What is the minimum number of resistors that were used, and what is the resistance of each resistor? [2 marks]

3. Fill in the 4th column of the table. [2 marks]

4. With the help of the above table, plot the characteristic of the source $V = f(i)$ on a system of rectangular axes. The horizontal axis is to be the current.

(a) From the above graph determine the electromotive force and the internal resistance of the source.

(b) From the values of the 4th column of the table, find the maximum power that the potato battery you studied can deliver.

(c) What must the external resistance of the circuit be so that the battery delivers the maximum power?

(d) How many such potato batteries would you have to make in order to operate an LED of power $1\,\mathrm{mW}$?

[1×4 = 4 marks]

problems.title: Problem 1
problems.problem:
A cruise ship of length $\ell = 160\,\mathrm{m}$ moves in the straight canal of the Isthmus of Corinth with constant speed $\upsilon_1 = 4$ knots (1 knot = 1 nautical mile per hour, or about $0.5\,\mathrm{m/s}$), towed by a tugboat. Under the conditions of the passage the surface of the water is calm, with no current in any direction. At the instant $t_0 = 0\,\mathrm{s}$ when the bow, the front part of the ship, reaches the exit of the canal, the tugboat withdraws and the ship accelerates with its engines, so that at the instant $t_1$ when the stern, the rear part of the ship, also reaches the exit of the canal its speed is $\upsilon_2 = 12$ knots.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2026-3-1-fig1.jpg

(a) Find the time interval $(0 - t_1)\,\mathrm{s}$ of the ship's exit from the canal.

(b) Find how much of the length of the ship is inside the canal at the instant $t_2 = \frac{t_1}{2}$.

(c) The length of the Isthmus is $L = 6340\,\mathrm{m}$. Find the total time that the motion of the ship inside the canal lasts.

[6+7+6 marks]

problems.title: Problem 2
problems.problem:
The Grade 10 (Α΄ Λυκείου) students and their physics teacher visited a ski resort to take part in an unusual competition. The aim of the competition was to descend a long run of inclination $\theta = 18^\circ$ in the longest possible time, so that the winner would be the one who made the slowest descent without stopping. The students, in groups, shared 4 identical sledges of mass $m_1 = 10\,\mathrm{kg}$, which they had painted red, blue, green and yellow, while for each colour respectively the coefficient of kinetic friction with the surface of the run was respectively equal to 0.15 / 0.20 / 0.25 and 0.30. On each sledge a student of mass $m_2 = 50\,\mathrm{kg}$ got on and, with an instantaneous push, acquiring the same initial velocity for all, began to descend the run in a straight line. Along the way the force due to the wind is horizontal, of magnitude $F = 40\,\mathrm{N}$, and directed so as to oppose the motion.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2026-3-2-fig1.jpg

(a) Which colour of sledge do you think won the competition of the slowest descent?

(b) One sledge did not manage to complete the course of the run, as it stopped. What was its colour?

Given: $\sin 18^\circ = 0.31$, $\cos 18^\circ = 0.95$, $g = 10\,\mathrm{\frac{m}{s^2}}$.

[2×10 marks]

problems.title: Problem 3
problems.problem:
An engineer is designing the specifications for the installation of a lift in a skyscraper. The maximum permitted mass of the cabin together with the passengers is $m = 3600\,\mathrm{kg}$. During the ascent the maximum speed is $\upsilon_1 = 15\,\mathrm{\frac{m}{s}}$, during the descent $\upsilon_2 = 12\,\mathrm{\frac{m}{s}}$, while the acceleration has the limit $|\alpha| = 1.2\,\mathrm{\frac{m}{s^2}}$. If friction during the motion is negligible, calculate:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2026-3-3-fig1.jpg

(a) The value of the maximum and of the minimum force with which the suspension cable of the cabin is stretched.

(b) The minimum time to cover the distance $s = 450\,\mathrm{m}$ from the ground floor to the top.

(c) The maximum and the minimum reading of a scale on the floor of the cabin, on which a passenger of mass $m_1 = 75\,\mathrm{kg}$ stands.

(d) The minimum time for the return from the top to the ground floor. $g = 10\,\mathrm{\frac{m}{s^2}}$.

[4×5 marks]

problems.title: Problem 4
problems.problem:
During a hunt a hunting dog is running with speed $\upsilon_1 = 4\,\mathrm{\frac{m}{s}}$ when it notices a hare at a distance $s = 6\,\mathrm{m}$. The dog is taken by surprise and acquires an acceleration $\alpha_1 = -0.20\,\mathrm{\frac{m}{s^2}}$ at the same instant as the hare takes to its heels with acceleration $\alpha_2 = 0.80\,\mathrm{\frac{m}{s^2}}$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2026-3-4-fig1.jpg

(a) Will the dog catch the hare, and if so at what distance? Comment on the choice of the result.

(b) If the acceleration of the frightened hare were $\alpha_3 = 1.80\,\mathrm{\frac{m}{s^2}}$, what would their minimum distance be? (The "disappointment" distance for the hunting dog.)

[2×10 marks]

problems.title: Problem 5A: Experimental study of free fall: determination of the constant g
problems.problem:
Experimental study of free fall: determination of the constant $g$

A group of students wants to study experimentally the free fall of a weight using a $50\,\mathrm{Hz}$ electronic timer and then to calculate the value of the constant $g$ of the acceleration of gravity. In addition they have a paper tape, on which the timer will mark the positions of the weight during the free fall, and a ruler for measuring the distances. The students carry out the experiment, measure the displacements and fill in the table below with data:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2026-3-5-fig1.jpg

[Labels in the photograph: Ηλεκτρικός χρονομετρητής = electric timer; Χαρτοταινία = paper tape; Βαρίδι = weight.]

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c} \text{Time } t\ (\mathrm{s}) & 0.00 & 0.02 & 0.04 & 0.06 & 0.08 & 0.10 & 0.12 & 0.14 \\ \hline \text{Displacement } y\ (\mathrm{cm}) & 0.0 & 0.1 & 0.7 & 1.7 & 3.1 & 4.8 & 6.8 & 9.3 \end{array}$$

A. Calculate the time interval $\Delta t$ between two successive strikes of the timer.

B. Which variables will you use to draw the graph from which you will calculate the constant $g$? Justify your answer.

C. Draw the appropriate graph and calculate the value of the constant $g$.

D. Convert the value of $g$ to S.I. units and calculate the relative error of the measurement with respect to the value $9.8\,\mathrm{\frac{m}{s^2}}$.

problems.title: Problem 5B
problems.problem:
On a table there is a digital data-acquisition and display system. The system has a distance sensor which emits ultrasound. The ultrasound, if it meets some obstacle, is reflected, and from the time of emission and reception the system calculates the distance of the object at which the ultrasound is reflected. Thus, with continuous operation, we can obtain a graph of the distance of an object from the detection system as a function of time. The system was put into operation and a student of mass $80\,\mathrm{kg}$ began to move in front of the system along a straight line. The graph produced by the system, after it was approximated by first- and second-degree functions, is the one below.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2026-3-6-fig1.jpg

The segments βγ, δε, ζη and θι are straight lines.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/greece-2026-3-6-fig2.png

1. From the above graph, describe the motion of the student.

2. Find the acceleration in the interval αβ.

3. Find the velocity in the interval βγ.

4. Find the acceleration in the intervals γδ, εζ and ηθ.

5. Find the net force acting on the student in the intervals αβ, δε and ηθ.

6. If the student were wearing skates with a coefficient of kinetic friction equal to 0.1, could he perform this particular motion?

7. Draw the graph of velocity and of acceleration against time.
